subject: english-language-arts
title: Launch and diagnostic: active reading habits
essential_question: How can understanding reading and writing community help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Activate prior knowledge about active reading habits, surface initial thinking without penalty, and establish the unit question.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of active reading habits.
Check, revise, or improve work about active reading habits using stated success criteria.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about active reading habits.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Present a brief, accessible prompt connected to “active reading habits.” Ask the learner to notice, predict, estimate, recall, or pose a question before instruction.

Read or listen closely, annotate or notice craft, discuss evidence, and create a written or spoken response for a real purpose. Keep the explanation centered on active reading habits. Name the success criteria and model how to check work or evidence.
Complete two supported examples or source-based tasks about active reading habits. After each step, ask: “What evidence or reasoning supports that move?” Fade prompts on the second example.
Learner completes a new application of active reading habits and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about active reading habits; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.

student_activity: Learner completes a new application of active reading habits and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about active reading habits; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence/reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for active reading habits, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for active reading habits works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of active reading habits, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking active reading habits mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use annotations, discussion notes, reading response, writing sample, revision, and transfer to a new text; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.
extension: Apply active reading habits under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Offer an alternate text or private response when content is personally sensitive.
Do not require autobiographical disclosure; fictionalized or analytical alternatives are always acceptable.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting active reading habits.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw private reflections, raw answers, voice recordings, or diagnosis language. For safety-critical tasks, record only the needed guardian confirmation.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of active reading habits in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, or private disclosure is required.

essential_question: How can understanding publication and communication capstone help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Practice editing conventions with prompts, feedback, and gradually reduced support.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of editing conventions.
Check, revise, or improve work about editing conventions using stated success criteria.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about editing conventions.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Present a brief, accessible prompt connected to “editing conventions.” Ask the learner to notice, predict, estimate, recall, or pose a question before instruction.

Read or listen closely, annotate or notice craft, discuss evidence, and create a written or spoken response for a real purpose. Keep the explanation centered on editing conventions. Name the success criteria and model how to check work or evidence.
Complete two supported examples or source-based tasks about editing conventions. After each step, ask: “What evidence or reasoning supports that move?” Fade prompts on the second example.
Learner completes a new application of editing conventions and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about editing conventions; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.

student_activity: Learner completes a new application of editing conventions and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about editing conventions; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence/reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for editing conventions, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for editing conventions works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of editing conventions, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking editing conventions mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use annotations, discussion notes, reading response, writing sample, revision, and transfer to a new text; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.
extension: Apply editing conventions under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Offer an alternate text or private response when content is personally sensitive.
Do not require autobiographical disclosure; fictionalized or analytical alternatives are always acceptable.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting editing conventions.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw private reflections, raw answers, voice recordings, or diagnosis language. For safety-critical tasks, record only the needed guardian confirmation.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of editing conventions in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, or private disclosure is required.
